evidence: Stirrings in the Jug, Class Notes, W.E.B. Du Bois and American Political Thought, and Race, Politics, and Culture are by or edited by Adolph Reed Jr. Renewing Black Intellectual History is his collaboration with Kenneth W. Warren. The Underclass as Myth and Symbol is also Reed’s.

Encountering the Sacred, Christian Gaza in Late Antiquity, The Monastic School of Gaza, and Prayer and Worship in Eastern Christianities are authored or coedited by Brouria Bitton-Ashkelony. Her university publication records also identify the listed prayer and pilgrimage articles. Bruria and Brouria are transliteration variants.

O Amazonas na época Imperial, A grande crise, Tempos de esperança, Síntese da História do Amazonas, and O Brazil acreano are Antônio José Souto Loureiro’s. The Manaus/T. Loureiro fragments fit his publisher. Biografia do Gen Pqdt Roberto de Pessôa is by Antônio Carlos Lobo Loureiro: about 16/17 listed citation weight belongs to the LC author.

A ciência dos trópicos, Exorcistas e demônios, Nem nobre, nem mecânico, and the thesis O paradoxo das luzes are Márcia Moisés Ribeiro’s. She also contributed to História ambiental paulista and A época pombalina no mundo luso-brasileiro; those entries retain the containing volumes. The display name is erroneous for these works.

Louisbourg from its foundation to its fall is John Stewart McLennan’s; the Halifax/Book Room and London/Macmillan fragments are editions of it (11 listed citation weight). The Aurora; its Spectrum and Spectroscopy of the Light from the Night Sky belong to physicist John Cunningham McLennan (2). LC share is about 11/13.

The Trade in Lunacy and The English Provincial Madhouse and Insanity are William Llywelyn Parry-Jones’s; the Hook Norton/Witney entry is also his. Boarding-out insane patients is coauthored with Harriet Sturdy. Bulimia and the 1994 Psychological Medicine article are coauthored with Brenda Parry-Jones. William Ll. abbreviates William Llywelyn.

Saúde e previdência, Hipólito José da Costa, Um monarca da fuzarca, and Os paradoxos da liberdade belong to Sérgio Goes de Paula as author, editor, or coauthor (11/13 listed citation weight). Fazenda do Centro is Sérgio Peres de Paula’s. The single Antologia do Correio Braziliense citation is ambiguous; estimated LC share is about 90%.

Vem do bairro do Jurunas, the 2006 Novos Cadernos NAEA and 2009 História Revista articles, and the Belém/Guamá chapters are Carmem Izabel Rodrigues’s (about 14/20 listed citation weight). The cartography works and Temporalidades item are Carmem Marques Rodrigues’s; História de Belo Horizonte is Carlos Rodrigues’s; Intelectuais & Comunismo is coedited by Cândido Moreira Rodrigues.

Médicos italianos em São Paulo is Maria do Rosário Rolfsen Salles’s. The Italian physicians article with Castro Santos, Polish immigration article with Sênia Bastos, and Imigrantes internacionais collection and chapters are also hers. Revista de Imigração e Colonização abbreviates her 2007 article’s title. The displayed Maria Izabel name is erroneous for these works.

On Individuality and Social Forms, The Web of Group Affiliation, O Estrangeiro, As grandes cidades e a vida do espírito, and the listed secrecy, ruin, religion, and exchange essays are Georg Simmel’s. George is a spelling variant in the citations; Exchange is included in the 1971 collection.
